biological.citation: SATB2 preserves colon stem cell identity and mediates ileum-colon conversion via enhancer remodeling (PMID: 34582804)
biological.summary: SATB2 is a colon-restricted chromatin factor that singularly preserves LGR5+ adult colonic stem cell and epithelial identity in mice and humans. Loss of Satb2 in adult mice leads to stable conversion of colonic stem cells into small intestine ileal-like stem cells, while SATB2 confers colonic properties on the mouse ileum. SATB2 regulates colonic identity by modulating enhancer binding of intestinal transcription factors CDX2 and HNF4A.

biological.citation: USP10 promotes glioma stem cell maintenance and glioblastoma growth by antagonizing DTX3L-mediated SATB2 ubiquitination (PMID: 41507172)
biological.summary: USP10 acts as a deubiquitinase and DTX3L acts as a ubiquitin ligase for SATB2 in glioma stem cells, regulating SATB2 ubiquitination at the K266 residue through mutually exclusive interactions. Knockdown of USP10 or overexpression of DTX3L markedly downregulates SATB2, inhibiting glioma stem cell self-renewal and GBM growth, which can be rescued by SATB2 overexpression. Pharmacological inhibition of USP10 by Wu-5 effectively suppresses tumor growth.

biological.citation: A critical period of translational control during brain development at codon resolution (PMID: 36482253)
biological.summary: Satb2 undergoes timed translational upregulation during mouse neocortex neurogenesis, restricting protein expression to neuronal lineages despite broad transcriptional priming in progenitors. This translational control of Satb2 is essential for neuronal subtype differentiation. Changing activity of eIF4EBP1 affects neurogenesis of the Satb2 lineage.

biological.citation: Protein translation rate determines neocortical neuron fate (PMID: 38849354)
biological.summary: Ire1α was identified as a regulator of Satb2 expression and neuronal polarity in a small molecule screening. Satb2 mRNA translation requires eIF4A1 helicase activity towards its 5'-untranslated region, demonstrating post-transcriptional regulation of SATB2. This places SATB2 as a key determinant of cortical neuron identity regulated by proteostasis mechanisms.

biological.citation: Satb2 Regulates EphA7 to Control Soma Spacing and Self-Avoidance of Cortical Pyramidal Neurons (PMID: 34546353)
biological.summary: RNA-seq of Satb2 conditional knockout mouse cortex revealed that EphA7 transcription is dramatically increased in layers II/III upon Satb2 loss. ChIP and luciferase reporter assays demonstrated direct suppression of EphA7 expression by Satb2. Overexpression of EphA7 in late-born cortical neurons phenocopied Satb2 knockdown (soma clumping and impaired self-avoidance), and reducing EphA7 rescued Satb2 knockdown phenotypes.

biological.citation: Ginkgolide a enhances the resistance to pathogen infection through mitochondrial unfolded protein response (PMID: 41055707)
biological.summary: DVE-1, a C. elegans homeodomain transcription regulator homologous to mammalian SATB2, mediates Ginkgolide A-enhanced innate immunity against both Gram-negative and Gram-positive pathogens. This function was shown to be conserved, as GA also protected lung epithelial cells and mice during P. aeruginosa infection via the homeodomain transcription factor SATB2. SATB2 thus participates in innate immune responses through the mitochondrial unfolded protein response pathway.

biological.citation: Multiomic profiling of transcription factor binding and function in human brain (PMID: 38831039)
biological.summary: ChIP-seq profiling in postmortem human brain tissues and sorted nuclei revealed that SATB2 binds unique genomic regions depleted for high-occupancy TF sites and promotes neuronal gene expression. SATB2 binding sites are enriched in neurons and regulate neuron-specific gene expression programs. This resource (BrainTF) provides genome-wide occupancy maps for SATB2 in human brain.

biological.citation: ASHG 2015 - Convergence of genes and pathways influencing neurodevelopment following suppression of ASD-associated chromatin modifiers and transcriptional regulators in human neural progenitor cells (S. Erdin et al.)
biological.summary: RNAi-mediated suppression of SATB2 in iPSC-derived neural progenitor cells (NPCs) was performed alongside suppression of CHD8, TCF4, and AUTS2. Statistically significant overlap was detected between genes regulated by SATB2 and those regulated by TCF4 and CHD8, with transcriptional consequences converging on cell adhesion and Wnt/Notch signaling networks enriched for ASD-associated genes.

biological.citation: ASHG 2012 - SATB2 Acts as an Activator of the UPF3B Gene (P. Leoyklang et al.)
biological.summary: Chromatin immunoprecipitation demonstrated that SATB2 protein binds to the promoter of the UPF3B gene, and luciferase reporter assays showed that recombinant SATB2 significantly activates UPF3B transcription. A SATB2 nonsense mutation produced a truncated protein that dimerized with wild-type SATB2 and interfered with its normal activity, causing a dominant negative effect. Patient leukocytes with the SATB2 mutation showed significantly decreased UPF3B mRNA levels.

biological.citation: ASHG 2023 - AlphaCluster: Coevolutionary driven residue-residue interaction models enable quantifiable clustering analysis of de novo variants to enhance predictions of pathogenicity (J. Obiajulu et al.)
biological.summary: Using the AlphaCluster method to analyze spatial clustering of de novo missense variants on protein tertiary structures, SATB2 was newly implicated at the genome-wide level in autism spectrum disorder. SATB2 was identified alongside GABBR2 as one of two genes newly associated with ASD, and was also among eleven genes implicated in neurodevelopmental disorders.
